# `silk/machine/generate`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Silk source from a `Definition`: the transition table of each chart as a static function.

## Details
The program owns its types: the state union, the event union, the context and the effects,
with the names `<Name>`, `<Name>Event`, `<Name>Context` and `<Name>Effect`, and one state
union per region chart, named after the chart. It also owns the guard functions, named
`guard<State><Event>` for a transition on an event and `when<State>` for an eventless one.
In the chart of a region the chart's name comes first: `guard<Chart><State><Event>` and
`when<Chart><State>`. The generated module imports all of them from the module passed as
`types` and declares one `pub static fn <chart>Chart()` per chart, which the program returns
from `Machine.chart` of that chart's state union.

The initial state and the target of a transition are written as values, such as
`Editor.Open { bold: Bold.Off, italic: Italic.Plain }`: the state, with each region at the
initial state of its chart. A state that holds data of its own cannot be generated, because
a definition does not have that data.

A state with a history gets a `Chart.history` or `Chart.shallowHistory` row that names a
field of the context, a `History` of the chart's state union, and a transition to the
history is written with `Chart.resume`.

Every state, event and region field name in the definition is checked against the unions
when the generated module is compiled, so a definition that names a state the program does
not have fails there.

## Gotchas
Several guarded transitions of one state on one event share one guard function name. Give
them one function, or edit the definition so that they differ.

Import as `Generate` with `import silk.machine.generate { Generate }`.

Public declarations: 1.
